headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP can leak or misroute prompts, while the pair also has clear shared-workflow conflict and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent exposes MCP over stdio/SSE and can run browsers/subprocesses, so it can ingest external content and pass it onward; the other agent is a docs/source-available prompt-leak corpus with no runtime defenses shown. A shared channel is not documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but the interaction is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards browser or MCP content into the other agent’s prompt stream, injection becomes reachable.
IF the two agents are bridged by copy-paste or a shared MCP endpoint, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of external text into prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all MCP payloads and reject untrusted instructions.
Use a manual review step before any content from one agent is reused by the other.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents behind separate workspaces or brokers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, and it has broad network egress plus API-key handling. The other agent has no runtime egress, but its docs indicate prompt-leak content. If they share a workspace or prompt channel, sensitive material from LightAgent can be exposed; the exact bridge is undocumented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents read the same workspace or clipboard, LightAgent data can be copied into the leak corpus.
IF LightAgent sends tool results or memory into external APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate OS users or containers.
Remove secrets from any shared prompt or file path.
Turn off automatic export of tool results and memory.
Review outbound destinations before enabling network egress.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on shared inputs and outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances, subprocesses, browsers, MCP, and broad egress, so concurrent writes or overlapping side effects are plausible. The other agent is non-runnable and has no write surface, which lowers direct conflict, but uncertainty about orchestration and shared state means the safer call is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LightAgent instances share a mutable workspace, they can race on files or workflow state.
IF the non-runnable agent is used as a source artifact in the same directory, concurrent edits can collide.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs when MCP tools mutate shared state.
Check for git or file conflicts before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool calls, results, and provenance metadata, which makes its outputs easy for another agent to treat as authoritative. The second agent is a prompt-leak repository rather than an evaluator, so it may amplify or preserve bad instructions instead of verifying them. Because the exact handoff is undocumented, this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF outputs from LightAgent are reused as prompts or facts, downstream errors can propagate.
IF the second agent is used to curate or relay those outputs without verification, mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require a human check before reusing one agent’s output in the other.
Separate factual outputs from instructions in different channels.
Add a validation step for citations, tool results, and file paths.
Reject outputs that contain imperative language unless explicitly expected.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles conversations, memory, and tool results, which can create retention or residency concerns. The other agent is source-available docs with no runtime data handling shown, so it is not the main compliance driver. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so this is a low-risk policy-gap assessment.
conditions: IF LightAgent is used with regulated data, its logging and memory handling must match the operator’s policy.
IF the docs repository is repurposed to store user content, retention rules may be violated.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into LightAgent until retention is reviewed.
Rotate any API keys used during testing.
Confirm logging and deletion settings before production use.
Keep the docs repository free of user content.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
